title: Fri 27 Nov · morning check
summary:

[b]Next:[/b] France Q3 GDP 09:45, US trade data and Canada current account 15:30, US half-day close 20:00 (Bucharest); OPEC+ Sunday.

USD.note: December Fed hike still priced near certainty (94–98%, grade C); no Fed speaker overnight; US half-day session today.

EUR.note: No new French step after the failed CMP; scenario E (N2 −2) gives −2; France GDP and CPI this morning.

GBP.note: No MPC remark overnight; scenario G (BoE hawks scored) gives +3.

JPY.note: Tokyo core CPI 2.9% vs 3.0% forecast, core-core 2.5%: the yen trigger (above 3.1%) not met; scenarios H +2, T −3, both 0.

CHF.note: No SNB item; tariff scenario T gives −1; VIX test at the US half-day close.

CAD.note: Brent settled $96.57 (+$1.96); BoC hike bets said to rise (no figure, C); no written trigger met.

AUD.note: RBA still silent after the hot CPI; scenario A gives +4.

NZD.note: Final count: coalition 65 seats, one short of a majority; N2 0 → −1 (shadow −3); new election possible.

XAU.note: Gold factor G +1 unchanged; spot near $3,565; no ETF or central-bank data.

pairs.note:
[b]📍 DAILY CHECK · Fri 27 Nov (morning)[/b]

[b]Tokyo inflation hit a 16-month high but still missed the forecast, so the yen did not get the hawkish push USDJPY was watching for.[/b]
Core CPI ex fresh food rose to 2.9% from 2.6%, just under the 3.0% expected, while the measure that also strips out energy eased to 2.5%. Energy did the lifting, which is not the broad inflation a December BoJ hike needs. The yen's written trigger, a print above 3.1%, was not met. The dollar leg is unchanged ahead of a half-day US session.
